title: API Business Logic and Reliable Workforce Processes
tagline: An API route is the entrance. Business rules decide which change is valid, authorized and still current.
problem: Staff requests could contain malformed rates, an invalid role or an outdated revision. A payroll packet that looked empty could still contain meaningful edits in a prior version. Saving JSON without these rules could overwrite decisions or discard important work.
solution: Separate route validation, trusted identity/role checks, pure business rules and the transactional store. Use actual wage-input/revision rules and complete payroll-draft history classification, with parameterized SQL/audit source shown separately.
outcome: The runnable example rejects unauthorized approvals and stale decisions before a store operation, and preserves the distinction between empty, meaningful and unknown draft history. It demonstrates how business rules protect operational records rather than merely returning HTTP success.
strengths: Pure rules can be checked without an HTTP server, Azure login or live database.
A stale revision or nonpending decision returns a conflict instead of silently overwriting newer work.
Draft classification examines every saved version and treats unknown shapes conservatively.
tests: Ten Node tests passed: two original discard tests and eight new focused tests over the actual extracted wage rules.
limit: The public runtime uses pure rules and a small error adapter. It does not validate JWTs, open SQL, prove distributed concurrency or complete a payroll transaction.
diagram:
UI[User action / JSON] --> Route[HTTP route]
  Route --> Auth[Verified identity / route permissions]
  Auth --> Rules[Input / role / state / revision rules]
  Rules --> Store[Parameterized SQL transaction]
  Store --> Audit[Business change + audit]
  Audit --> Response[Useful success / validation / conflict response]
